### Observed differences

- In the later window, four activities that were almost unobserved before — A19, A20, A25 and A26, each present in at most 1 of 200 earlier traces — appear in about 43–62 of 200 traces (roughly 21–31% participation). A06 also roughly doubles, from about 23 to about 56 of 200 traces (about 12% to 28%). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- The routing out of A42 changed almost completely: before, about 92 in 100 of A42's outgoing transitions went directly to A27; in the later window almost none do, and about 98 in 100 go to one of A19 (about 29%), A20 (about 26%), A26 (about 23%) or A25 (about 20%). [DIR006]
- The four activities behave as mutually exclusive alternatives: their participations (about 31%, 26%, 22% and 23%) sum to roughly the full window while any two of them co-occur in at most about 1 in 100 later traces, so nearly every later trace contains exactly one of them. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL014, REL015, REL020]
- Each alternative is embedded between A42 and A27: A42 precedes the chosen activity and the chosen activity precedes A27 in nearly every trace containing it (for example, A19 precedes A27 in about 30 of 100 traces against 31% participation), each alternative's own outgoing transitions now lead to A27 in about 95–98 in 100 of cases, and the A42-to-A27 distance moved from one event (about 92% of earlier traces) to two events (about 97% of later traces). [REL010, REL011, REL016, REL017, REL021, REL022, REL025, REL026, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG002]
- The four alternatives sit at about one third of the trace (mean relative positions roughly 0.35–0.37), just ahead of A27, whose position is essentially unchanged (mean about 0.38 before, 0.40 after); A27 and A47 appear in every trace in both windows with nearly unchanged positions. [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007]
- A06 moved from a mid-trace role to a late one: its mean relative position rose from about 0.46 to about 0.89 (median about 0.97), and in the later window about 86 in 100 of its outgoing transitions go to A48, adjacent within one event in about 98 in 100 of the roughly 50 traces containing both; before, its successors were spread over many activities (largest share about 17% to A15) and only about 8 in 100 went to A48. [OCC001, DIR001, POS001, LAG001]
- A47 now leads to A06 in about 24 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 1 in 100 before), and the A47-to-A48 distance shifted from one event in about 96% of earlier traces to two events in about 24% of later traces, matching A06 sitting between A47 and A48; A27 also precedes A06 in about 26 of 100 later traces versus about 5–6 of 100 before. [DIR007, LAG003, REL005, REL006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, the passage between A42 and A27 runs through one of four mutually exclusive activities — A19, A20, A25 or A26 — replacing the previously direct A42-to-A27 transition in nearly every trace, and that A06 has additionally taken on a late-trace role immediately before A48, sitting directly between A47 and A48 in about a quarter of traces. Behaviourally, A42 now feeds the four alternatives in about 98 of 100 of its outgoing transitions, each alternative in turn precedes A27, and A06 appears in about 28% of traces (up from about 12%) almost always followed by A48. [DIR006, REL010, REL016, REL021, REL025, LAG002, DIR001, LAG001, DIR007, LAG003]

The order and placement claims rest on direct relational and adjacency evidence rather than participation alone, and the occurrence, routing, position, relation and lag indicators all describe one coherent picture; the scale of the shifts (the four activities from at most 1 in 200 traces to 43–62 in 200, the direct A42-to-A27 share from about 92% to about 0) and the number of qualifying items (50 versus roughly 0.69 expected if nothing had changed) are far beyond what random re-splits of stable behaviour produce. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006, REL010, LAG002]

Limitations remain: the earlier routing of A19, A20 and A26 rests on a single trace each and A25 was not observed at all before, so their prior behaviour is not reliably known; the exact split of traffic among the four alternatives and the small new edges of about 2 in 100 could partly reflect sampling differences in variant frequencies between the finite windows; and the evidence cannot show whether the rerouting around A42 and the changed role of A06 are one coordinated modification or two independent ones, since several items describe the same underlying trace behaviour rather than independent confirmations. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR005, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
